simple.meaning: בַּעַר (baʻar) is a Hebrew word meaning “properly, foot (as consumed); i.e. (by exten.) of cattle brutishness ; (concretely) stupid.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: בַּעַר (H1198) appears 5 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Psalms 49:11, with occurrences in Psalms, Proverbs.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to בַּעַר (H1198) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in בַּעַר (H1198) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: בַּעַר (baʻar) / H1198 is traced through Psalms 49:11, Psalms 73:22, Psalms 92:7, Proverbs 12:1 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.short: properly, foot (as consumed); i.e. (by exten.) of cattle brutishness ; (concretely) stupid
definitions.full: H1198. baar בַּ֫עַר noun masculine brutishness (only in poetry) — absolute ׳ב Psa 49:11 3 t., בָּ֑עַר Prov 12:1 ; — combination, ׳אִישׁבֿ brutish man Psa 92:7 (|| כסיל ); elsewhere ׳ב alone in same sense (concrete) 49:11 (|| id. ), & as predicate = adjective, 73:22 ; Prov 12:1 ; 30:2 .
